text:
Sasha: Quick question — we're still letting requests with no workspace header fall back to the shared pool if the token has no workspace claim. That behavior is causing cross-tenant routing for some private endpoint customers. Can we discuss making gateway enforce workspace scoping for dedicated pools? @Maya @Elliot
Maya: IIRC we kept the header-less fallback for legacy clients and because some customers use VPC-only auth which doesn't embed workspace in tokens. Changing it will break them. :thinking:
Elliot: Proposal: enforce strict scoping only for private/dedicated endpoints. Routing precedence: 1) VPC endpoint mapping -> 2) token.claims.workspace_id -> 3) X-Workspace header -> 4) workspace default -> 5) reject. That way hosted API stays permissive.
Priya: If gateway rejects, we need a clear error so apps can migrate. Also we should pair enforcement with quota checks — dedicated pools must have tenant quotas enforced by gateway to avoid noisy neighbors.
Sasha: +1 on clear error. Suggest a migration mode: "log-only" for 2 weeks, metric counts, then 30% canary enforce, then full enforce. We need telemetry to show "would-be" rejects per workspace.
Ken: From console UX POV we should add a toggle per-dedicated-pool: "Strict workspace scoping" (off/soft/on). Soft = log-only, On = block. Console should show a small rollout slider (0-100%) and a chart of affected requests.
Elliot: Implementation detail — we can inject an internal header early: X-Redwood-Workspace-Affinity when token claim present; that helps downstream runtimes and quota checks. But for private endpoints where tokens don't have claims, we need to map by VPC subnet->workspace mapping or explicitly require workspace header.
Maya: We must keep backward compat path for customers using legacy cert-based auth. Maybe a per-workspace allowlist for "legacy mode" so we don't break cert-only clients. That list can be turned off during enforcement window.
Priya: Telemetry request: expose metric labels: routing_result={allowed|would_reject|rejected}, routing_source={token|header|vpc|default}, pool_type={shared|dedicated}. Also a daily rollup per workspace and sample payloads for debugging.
Sasha: Agree. Also add an audit log entry with request id when we transition to block mode. That saves debugging time for customers.
Ken: UX question — show a one-click migration plan in console: (1) enable soft, (2) view metrics for 2 weeks, (3) start canary, (4) enforce. And surface a list of top callers that will break.
Elliot: One more safety net: automatic fallback routing to a "quarantine" dedicated pool that has strict quota and rate limits, rather than dropping traffic immediately during canary. That reduces customer outages.
route-bot: deploy started for gateway-routing v2 (sha: a1b2c3) — feature flag: strict_workspace_scoping.rolling=0%
Maya: I'll own the migration docs. Can someone add the metric names to the observability board? @Priya ?
Priya: On it. I'll create dashboards with the routing_result and routing_source breakdowns and the per-workspace heatmap.
Sasha: Thanks — plan looks good. Next steps: implement header injection + logging, console toggle + rollout slider, telemetry, and docs. We'll sync in Tuesday eng-platform sync for rollout dates.
